chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 280 — Lü Xiucai's First Taste of Power & Li Huowang's Hidden Fear
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang secures travel permits but can't shake his paranoia. Lü Xiucai masters a Luo Sect technique—and his arrogance proves power without wisdom is a dangerous thing.
og_title: Chapter 280: The Price of Divine Power
og_description: A quiet chapter with sharp edges. Li Huowang gets his travel papers, the troupe earns real money, and Lü Xiucai learns that power can poison faster than it can save.
twitter_title: Ch. 280: Lü Xiucai's Arrogance Is Already Showing
twitter_description: Travel permits secured, a new opera earning good silver, and a disciple who thinks he's already above his own family. The calm before the storm.

lore_anchors.definition: An official document required for travel between cities in imperial China; without one, outsiders could be detained as vagrants or bandits. In the Dao-Twisted World, it also serves as a temporary identity document.

A Ming Dynasty folk religious sect blending Chan Buddhism, Daoism, and folk belief; its scriptures were written in simple language for the illiterate. In the novel, its techniques offer dangerous shortcuts to power.
A ritual Daoist weapon made of 108 coins strung on red thread, used for exorcism and spiritual combat. In the Dao-Twisted World, its techniques are useless without the physical sword.
The lowest tier of the traditional Chinese social hierarchy, including actors, prostitutes, and servants. Lü Xiucai's contempt for his father's troupe reflects this deep social stigma.
A face-covering woven from old Chinese coins; in the Dao-Twisted World, it conceals the wearer's supernatural identity from spiritual perception.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why doesn't Li Huowang just wear the copper coin mask all the time?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He does when awake, but he knows it's a flimsy defense—he needs another layer of identity protection urgently.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Lü Xiucai's technique actually dangerous?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The technique itself seems clean, but it's useless without the bronze coin sword. His arrogance, however, is already a liability.
A mysterious figure from chinese folklore who offers goods on credit, with payment due when a prophecy comes true. In this world, he acts as a liaison to the Supervisory Heavenly Office.
